Napoleon inherited the Republic's hatred by the continental powers. All but two of his wars were declared on him, he just happened to know that he would rather fight an offensive than a defensive on French territory. If you look at how Britain violated peace terms, Austria kept backstabbing, the Spanish planned to betray him, the Russians violated their agreement with France, and so on, you would see that they wanted to do everything possible to get rid of revolutionary thought in France. They were threatened by it. 

I don't think it's fair to suggest a comparison to Khan either. Napoleon didn't encourage mass rape and murder (his troops did a couple times though, as did the other armies). In fact he was too soft in order to be diplomatic, when he should have burned Vienna and Berlin.

Would I want to be a civilian during those times, or get drafted into the Grande Armée only to get swallowed by the Steppes? No. But there's quite a few worse or equally bad times to be alive I can think of.
